purpose: An adapter declares the core version it supports twice: once in its Python
distribution metadata (what pip enforces) and once in the package-environment
requirement its studio resolver reads. The second declaration is hand-written
and drifts, so the resolver can select a core release the adapter explicitly
excluded on PyPI. This contract makes the second declaration derivable from the
first and gives both sides one machine-readable definition of the bound.

open_ceiling.reason: Core is still 0.x, so '<1.0.0' excludes nothing that exists. It is a placeholder copied from the compatibility matrix, not a release the adapter was verified against. Adapters should move to the next minor above the highest core minor they verified.

notes: The '..' range operator is exclusive at the upper end, so it maps directly
onto PEP 440 '<'. An inclusive ceiling ('<=') has no equivalent token and is
rejected instead of being widened. A truncated version is read as a prefix

wider_than_declared.description: The package-environment requirement must never admit a core release the Python distribution metadata excludes.

open_ceiling.description: The declared ceiling is the 1.0.0 placeholder rather than a verified next-minor bound.

unparseable.description: A declared requirement that cannot be parsed is treated as a violation, never as an exemption.

survey.source: public PyPI metadata compared against published package-environment requirements
survey.note: The only adapter versions still carrying both bounds were older releases, which shows the ceiling was lost during version evolution rather than never declared.

known_violations.note: Bounds agree with the declared range, but the ceiling is the 1.0.0 placeholder rather than a verified release, so the open_ceiling warning applies.
